artiest/myung-whun-chung.text:
Myung-whun Chung is a South Korean conductor and pianist, born on 22 January 1953. He studied piano with Maria Curcio and in 1974 won a shared second prize at the International Tchaikovsky Competition. With his sisters, the violinist Kyung-wha Chung and the cellist Myung-wha Chung, he played in the Chung Trio. He then studied conducting at Mannes College and at the Juilliard School.

He has conducted almost all the major orchestras of Europe and America, including the Berliner Philharmoniker, the Wiener Philharmoniker, the Los Angeles Philharmonic and the Metropolitan Opera in New York. From 1984 to 1990 he was chief conductor of the Rundfunk-Sinfonieorchester Saarbrücken. From 1989 to 1994 he was music director of the Opéra de Paris and opened the first season of the new Opéra Bastille with the complete Les Troyens by Berlioz, which the critics praised highly. In 1991 he was named Artist of the Year in France and in 1992 he received the Legion of Honour. He conducted the world premiere of Messiaen's last work, the Concert à quatre, which the composer dedicated to him and the Orchestre de la Bastille.

In 1997 Chung became artistic director of the Asia Philharmonic Orchestra and in 2000 of the Orchestre philharmonique de Radio France. The Tokyo Philharmonic Orchestra made him an honorary member, and in 2012 he became the first principal guest conductor in the history of the Staatskapelle Dresden. He shows how East Asian musicians in the late twentieth century won a leading place in Western classical music.
artiest/myung-whun-chung.listen: Listen to a recording in which Chung conducts a large orchestra, for example a Romantic work by Berlioz, and notice how the orchestra as a whole can grow from very soft to very loud.

artiest/n-dea-davenport.text:
N'Dea Davenport is an American singer, songwriter, dancer and producer, born on 22 September 1966. She was the lead singer of the British acid jazz band The Brand New Heavies and made a pioneering contribution to the genre. She graduated from Clark Atlanta University and then moved to Los Angeles, where she worked in stage productions and music videos.

In 1988 she began as a session singer and sang backing vocals for various artists. In 1989 came her debut as a guest singer on rapper Tone Lōc's Cheeba Cheeba, from the album Lōc-ed After Dark. This earned her a contract with his label Delicious Vinyl. That year she also sang on albums by, among others, Malcolm McLaren, Def Jef and Belinda Carlisle.

In 1990 the band The Brand New Heavies chose her, on the advice of the owners of Delicious Vinyl, as their singer to replace Jaye Ella Ruth. The group re-recorded its debut album with Davenport. In 1991 that re-recording was released on Delicious Vinyl. The album reached number twenty-four in the British album chart. The singles Dream Come True, Stay This Way and Don't Let It Go to Your Head were re-released with her vocals and all three reached the British top forty. Thanks to this success the band appeared on Soul Train, Showtime at the Apollo and Top of the Pops. In 1998 her solo album N'dea Davenport was released. Her warm, soulful voice helped give acid jazz, a mixture of jazz, funk and soul, a large audience.
artiest/n-dea-davenport.listen: Listen to Dream Come True by The Brand New Heavies and notice how her supple singing glides over the funky accompaniment.

artiest/n-w-a.text:
N.W.A was a hip hop group from Compton, a district of Los Angeles. Eazy-E, who had founded the label Ruthless Records with Jerry Heller, brought the group together in 1987. He worked with the producers Dr. Dre and Arabian Prince and with the rapper Ice Cube. DJ Yella and MC Ren joined later. The rappers told of life in their neighbourhood: poverty, gangs, drugs, racism and police violence.

In January 1989 Straight Outta Compton was released. The album opens with three tracks that set the tone: the title track introduces the group, Fuck tha Police protests against police violence and the stopping of people because of their skin colour, and Gangsta Gangsta sketches the worldview of young people from the city. Dr. Dre, DJ Yella and Arabian Prince made the beats, with hard drums and samples from funk and soul. The group itself called it reality rap, but it became known as gangsta rap. Fuck tha Police brought a warning letter from the FBI, and police officers refused to provide security at concerts. That uproar only made the group better known.

The lyrics were also controversial because they demeaned women and gay people and glorified crime. Many radio stations did not play the music. Even so, N.W.A sold millions of records and the group also reached a white audience. Ice Cube left at the end of 1989, and after Niggaz4Life (1991) the group broke up. Dr. Dre, Ice Cube and Eazy-E became successful solo. N.W.A gave rap a hard, political voice and influenced generations of hip hop artists.
artiest/n-w-a.listen: Listen to Fuck tha Police and notice how the track is built like a trial, in which the rappers testify against the police one by one. Hear how the hard beat and the angry voices give the lyrics their force.

artiest/nacio-herb-brown.text:
Nacio Herb Brown (1896 to 1964) was an American composer of popular songs, film music and music for Broadway, active from the 1920s to the early 1950s. He was born Ignacio Herbert Brown in Deming, New Mexico. In 1901 the family moved to Los Angeles. He received his first music lessons from his mother.

Brown first had a tailor's shop and then became a successful real estate agent, but he always wrote and played music. After his first hit, Coral Sea, in 1920 and a big hit, When Buddha Smiles, in 1921, he eventually became a full-time composer. In 1926 he joined ASCAP and wrote the piano piece The Doll Dance, followed by Rag Doll in 1928 and The Wedding of the Painted Doll in 1929.

In 1928 MGM hired him to write music in Hollywood for the new sound film. He often worked there with the lyricist Arthur Freed. His best-known work is the score of the musical film Singin' in the Rain of 1952, in which many of their songs return. He also appeared in The Hollywood Revue of 1929. On Broadway he worked with Richard Whiting and Buddy DeSylva, including on Take a Chance. Together with L. Wolfe Gilbert he wrote the music for the children's Western Hopalong Cassidy on television, which began in 1949. His songs show how Hollywood, in the transition from silent film to sound film, made a kind of pop of its own.
artiest/nacio-herb-brown.listen: Listen to the title song of Singin' in the Rain and notice how cheerful and simple the melody is, and how well the song suits a dance step.

artiest/nadia-boulanger.text:
Nadia Boulanger (1887 to 1979) was a French teacher, conductor and composer. She was born in Paris, into a musical family: her father Ernest and her sister Lili were respected composers. Her mother was a Russian princess. She entered the Conservatoire de Paris at an early age, but because she believed she had no special talent for composition, she stopped composing and became a teacher.

As a teacher she influenced generations of young composers, especially from the United States and other English-speaking countries. Her pupils included more than two hundred and fifty important composers, soloists, arrangers and conductors, among them Aaron Copland, Elliott Carter, Philip Glass, Quincy Jones, Astor Piazzolla, Daniel Barenboim and John Eliot Gardiner. She taught at, among others, the Juilliard School, the Yehudi Menuhin School, the Royal College of Music and the Royal Academy of Music, but her most important place was her parents' apartment in Paris, where she taught for almost seventy years, until her death at the age of ninety-two.

Boulanger was the first woman to conduct many major orchestras in America and Europe, including the BBC Symphony, the Boston Symphony, the Hallé and the Philadelphia Orchestra. She also led world premieres, including of work by Copland and Stravinsky. Her influence extends to pop music: her pupils helped write the film music, the jazz and the pop music of the twentieth century, and a tribute record calls her by her nickname, Dear Mademoiselle.
artiest/nadia-boulanger.listen: Listen to Faure: Requiem or to the recording In Memoriam Lili Boulanger and notice how restrained and clear the voices are brought together.

artiest/naftule-brandwein.text: Naftule Brandwein came from Galicia and emigrated to New York around 1909, where at first he played as an anonymous soloist in Abe Schwartz's band. From 1922 he made records under his own name, including for Victor. His clarinet playing was wild and full of trills, glides and leaps, with influences from Greek, Turkish and Roma music. On stage he was an exuberant showman.
artiest/naftule-brandwein.listen: Listen to Fihren Di Mechutonim Aheim, a piece for escorting the parents of the bride and groom home, and hear the clarinet laugh, weep and scream.

artiest/naseer-shamma.text:
Naseer Shamma is an Iraqi musician and oud player, the Arabic lute. He was born in 1963 in Kut, a city on the Tigris. At the age of twelve he began his oud studies in Baghdad, following in the footsteps of Jamil and Munir Bashir. In 1987 he obtained his diploma at the Baghdad Academy of Music. Three years later he began teaching himself, alongside his own studies. He wrote music for film, theatre and television and founded the Arabic Oud House.

In the 1980s the Iraqi government accused him of criticising Saddam Hussein. He was invited to the Iraqi embassy in Amman, abducted there and taken to Iraq against his will, where he was imprisoned, interrogated for weeks and sentenced to death without a trial. In the end he was released without any proceedings. He was later appointed UNESCO Artist for Peace and goodwill ambassador of the Red Crescent and the Red Cross.

His albums include The Moon Fades (2004), Maqamat Ziryab (2005), Hilal (2006), Land of Darkness (2010) and Viaje de las almas (Travelling Souls) (2011). As an oud player he continues the Iraqi tradition of the Bashirs, in which the oud as a solo instrument, with maqam, the Arabic melodic modes, has an important place. In 2024 he held his first art exhibition, Half Life.
artiest/naseer-shamma.listen: Listen to Sukûn al-layl fî Baghdad and notice how the oud makes the melody move with short ornaments. Can you hear how the musician lets the silence between the notes play its part?

artiest/nat-adderley.text:
Nat Adderley (1931 to 2000) was an American jazz trumpeter and composer, the younger brother of the saxophonist Julian Cannonball Adderley, with whom he played for years. He was born in Tampa, Florida, and grew up in Tallahassee, where his parents taught at Florida A&M University. His father had played trumpet professionally in his youth and passed his instrument on to Cannonball. When Cannonball switched to alto saxophone, he gave the trumpet to Nat, who began in 1946. In 1950 he switched to cornet. From 1951 to 1953 he was in the army and played in the army band under his brother.

After his service he studied at Florida A&M again, intending to become a teacher. When Lionel Hampton played there, Nat played for him and was invited to join his band, in which he played in 1954 and 1955 and toured Europe. The turning point came in 1955 in New York. At Café Bohemia, where the bassist Oscar Pettiford was playing, Cannonball was allowed to sit in and overwhelmed the musicians. Nat was then also brought on stage, with the same effect. Offers came in and that year he recorded for the first time, with records such as Introducing Nat Adderley and Bohemia After Dark.

The brothers moved to New York and founded a bop group. Nat wrote Work Song, from 1960, which became a jazz standard and also a success in the pop charts, after Oscar Brown Jr. wrote lyrics for it. His work shows how soulful hard bop in the 1960s also reached an audience outside jazz.
artiest/nat-adderley.listen: Listen to Work Song and notice how the simple, bluesy melody is repeated again and again and the band keeps grooving calmly underneath.

artiest/nat-king-cole.text:
Nat King Cole was born in 1919 as Nathaniel Adams Coles in Montgomery, Alabama. He grew up in Chicago, where his father was a Baptist minister and his mother a church organist. She taught him to play the organ. From the age of twelve he had piano lessons in jazz, gospel and classical music. At the end of the 1930s he began as a jazz pianist and formed the King Cole Trio. In the 1940s it was the best-selling act on the label Capitol Records, and the only Black act there. The trio was regarded as a model for later small jazz bands.

Straighten Up and Fly Right from 1943 is among the well-known songs of that period. From 1950 Cole opted for a career as a solo singer. He then had hits such as Unforgettable, Mona Lisa, Nature Boy, When I Fall in Love and Smile. His Christmas album The Christmas Song from 1960 became the best-selling Christmas album of that decade. He also recorded records in Spanish, such as Cole español.

From 1956 to 1957 he hosted The Nat King Cole Show, the first national television programme on NBC with a Black host. Despite his success he faced severe discrimination. He was a member of the NAACP and took part in the March on Washington in 1963. His singing is warm and calm, and his piano playing is full of jazz. In this way he linked the world of jazz with that of pop. He died in 1965. His daughter Natalie Cole sang his songs in 1991 on Unforgettable... with Love.
artiest/nat-king-cole.listen: Listen to Straighten Up and Fly Right. Notice the relaxed singing and how the small ensemble, with few instruments, still swings.

artiest/natalie-holt.text: Natalie Holt (born in 1982) studied violin at the Royal Academy of Music and then film composition at the National Film and Television School. She played in a string quartet and wrote music for British television, such as Three Girls (2017). For the Marvel series Loki (2021) she made a score with a large orchestra, a choir, synthesizers and the theremin, an electronic instrument that you play without touching it. It gives the deceptive god a strange, elusive sound. With Obi-Wan Kenobi (2022) she became the first woman to write the music for a live-action Star Wars production. John Williams supplied the main theme for it.
artiest/natalie-holt.listen: In the Loki music, notice the floating, gliding tone of the theremin and the sound of a solemn choir with synthesizers.

artiest/nathan-evans.text:
Nathan Evans is a Scottish folk and country singer, born on 19 December 1994. Before becoming a musician he worked as a postman for Royal Mail in Airdrie, a town east of Glasgow. He attended Caldervale High School and has a university degree in web design. He began playing guitar at the age of eight. He was a fan of Blink-182, Bob Dylan, Van Morrison and Paul Simon, and later was influenced by Lewis Capaldi and Ed Sheeran.

In 2020 he became known by posting videos on TikTok in which he sang sea shanties. Earlier he had already put pop and folk songs on the platform. In 2021 he released his version of the folk song Wellerman, which topped the British singles chart and also charted in several other countries. His debut album Wellerman: The Album was released in 2022 and did reasonably well in continental Europe. In Germany it reached number twelve. In 2024 1994 followed, which entered at number one in Scotland and, with the single Heather on the Hill, received a silver certification from the BPI. In January 2026 Angels' Share was released, an album with Saint Phnx.

Evans said in a 2023 BBC documentary that he had struggled with his mental health. His breakthrough shows how a social medium could, in a short time, turn an old song, a sea shanty that was passed on by word of mouth for generations, into a worldwide hit.
artiest/nathan-evans.listen: Listen to Wellerman and notice how the song builds: first a single voice, then more and more voices and sound, until a whole ship seems to be singing.

artiest/national-philharmonic-orchestra.text:
The National Philharmonic Orchestra was a British orchestra that existed solely for recordings. Charles Gerhardt, producer and conductor at RCA Records, founded it with the orchestra leader and contractor Sidney Sax. The occasion was, among other things, a large recording project for Reader's Digest. The orchestra began in 1964 under varying names, such as RCA Victor Symphony Orchestra and London Promenade, which consisted almost entirely of members of the London Philharmonic Orchestra. In 1971 it was registered as the National Philharmonic Orchestra.

Gerhardt and Sax drew musicians from the large London pool. The violins regularly included leaders of all the major London orchestras. At first the orchestra recorded only for RCA, from 1974 also for Decca, and from 1975 for Columbia. Many conductors worked with the orchestra, among them Leopold Stokowski, Riccardo Chailly, Richard Bonynge, Michael Kamen and Loris Tjeknavorian. Bonynge recorded all three of Tchaikovsky's ballets for Decca, and Kamen recorded the orchestral parts for Eric Clapton's concerts 24 Nights at the Royal Albert Hall.

Best known is the series Classic Film Scores, which Gerhardt made with the producer George Korngold for RCA, with titles such as Casablanca: Classic Film Scores for Humphrey Bogart, The Fantasy Film World of Bernard Herrmann and Psycho. For many listeners these are the first introduction to film music on record, with a rich orchestral sound in stereo. In this way the orchestra brought classic film music to a large audience, outside the cinema.
artiest/national-philharmonic-orchestra.listen: Listen to Psycho in the orchestra's recording and notice how the strings build tension with short, sharp strokes.

artiest/naushad.text: Naushad Ali grew up in Lucknow and became acquainted with Hindustani classical music and the folk music of North India. In the 1930s he moved to Bombay, where he worked his way up in film music. His great breakthrough was Rattan (1944). Naushad based many film songs on classical ragas. In Baiju Bawra (1952) Mohammed Rafi sings Man Tadpat Hari Darshan Ko Aaj in raga Malkauns. For Mother India (1957) and the historical epic Mughal-e-Azam (1960) he wrote large song scenes with chorus and orchestra. In it Lata Mangeshkar sings Pyar Kiya To Darna Kya. Naushad linked the classical tradition with popular Hindi film.
artiest/naushad.listen: Notice the classical melodic turns of the raga in the singing and the accompaniment with tabla, sitar and strings.

artiest/ndr-chor.text:
The NDR Chor, since 2021 the NDR Vokalensemble, is the choir of the North German broadcaster Norddeutscher Rundfunk, based in Hamburg. It was founded on 1 May 1946 as the choir of the Nordwestdeutscher Rundfunk and received its present name in 1956, when the broadcaster was split into NDR and WDR. The first director was Max Thurn, who chose fifty-five singers from more than two thousand applications from professional singers. Today it is a group of twenty-eight singers, and one of the best professional chamber choirs in Germany. The artistic director since 2019 is Klaas Stok.

In the early years the choir worked a great deal with the broadcaster's symphony orchestra. In 1948 it took part in a recording of Beethoven's Fidelio under Hans Schmidt-Isserstedt. The choir took part in groundbreaking projects, such as the concert premiere of Arnold Schönberg's Moses und Aron. Under Helmut Franz, director from 1965, more contemporary music came in. In 1967 he conducted the premiere of Ligeti's Lux aeterna, and there were premieres of Penderecki's Utrenja, Henze's oratorio Floß der Medusa, which caused a scandal, and Stockhausen's Atmen gibt das Leben.

Later the emphasis was on a cappella music from all periods, including all of Johannes Brahms's a cappella works. The choir showed how a broadcasting choir could carry, alongside the classical repertoire, the newest music of its time, sometimes with serious consequences.
artiest/ndr-chor.listen: Listen to Ligeti's Lux aeterna and notice how the voices slide into one another very slowly, until the sound becomes almost one great curtain of sound.

artiest/ne-yo.text:
Ne-Yo is the stage name of Shaffer Chimere Smith, born on 18 October 1979. He is an American singer, songwriter, producer and actor. He first gained recognition as a songwriter, after writing Let Me Love You for Mario in 2004. That success led in 2005 to a contract with Def Jam Recordings, then headed by Jay-Z. He is regarded as one of the most important faces of 2000s R&B and won three Grammys.

His breakthrough as an artist came with So Sick, from 2005, which reached the top of the Billboard Hot 100 in 2006. When You're Mad and Sexy Love followed, before his debut album In My Own Words in 2006. It went straight to number one on the Billboard 200, received praise from the critics and two Grammy nominations. His second and third albums, Because of You in 2007 and Year of the Gentleman in 2008, also did well. Because of You won a Grammy for best contemporary R&B album. The singles Because of You, Closer and Miss Independent reached the American top ten, and Miss Independent won two Grammys.

Libra Scale was released in 2010, and after that he left Def Jam for Motown. R.E.D. followed in 2012, then Non-Fiction, GOOD MAN, Another Kind of Christmas and Self Explanatory. Ne-Yo shows how a songwriter behind the scenes could grow into a star, with smooth, melodic R&B in the tradition of the great soul singers.
artiest/ne-yo.listen: Listen to So Sick and notice how the singing begins softly and almost spoken, and how simple the accompaniment is, so that his voice gets all the space.

artiest/ned-washington.text:
Ned Washington (1901 to 1976) was an American lyricist, born Edward Michael Washington in Scranton, Pennsylvania. He began in vaudeville as a master of ceremonies and started his career as a songwriter with Earl Carroll's Vanities on Broadway at the end of the 1920s. In 1930 he joined ASCAP. In 1934 MGM hired him and he moved to Hollywood, where he eventually wrote complete scores for feature films. In the 1940s he worked for several studios, including Paramount, Warner Brothers, Disney and Republic.

He collaborated with many of the great composers of his time, such as Hoagy Carmichael, Victor Young, Max Steiner and Dimitri Tiomkin. With Leigh Harline he wrote most of the melodic songs of the Pinocchio soundtrack, including When You Wish Upon a Star. For this he won the Oscar for best original song in 1940. In 1952 he won another Oscar for High Noon (Do Not Forsake Me, Oh My Darlin'). In total he received eleven Oscar nominations between 1940 and 1962.

His songs also include Rawhide, with music by Tiomkin, Town Without Pity, Wild Is the Wind and The 3:10 to Yuma. From 1957 until his death he was a board member of ASCAP. He was inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame and in 2001 was posthumously named a Disney Legend. His lyrics show how film songs from Hollywood, from cartoon to Western, shaped the popular music of the twentieth century.
artiest/ned-washington.listen: Listen to When You Wish Upon a Star from Pinocchio and notice how simple the words are, and how the melody gives the lyrics a feeling of hope.

artiest/nederlands-blazers-ensemble.text:
The Nederlands Blazers Ensemble is a wind ensemble made up of musicians from major Dutch symphony orchestras. It was founded in 1959 by Thom de Klerk, principal bassoonist of the Concertgebouw Orchestra. At the Amsterdam conservatory he had formed a student wind quintet with Martine Bakker, Edo de Waart, George Pieterson, Joep Terwey and Jaap Verhaar. De Klerk wanted to expand the group to play serenades for winds by, among others, Mozart and Dvořák, and to make it the I Musici of wind players. The core was an octet with two oboes, two clarinets, two bassoons and two horns, but the group was often larger.

After De Klerk's death in 1966 Edo de Waart took over his role. In that period the ensemble made many recordings and several composers wrote for the group. After De Waart left in 1975 it played without a conductor, and from 1985 to 1988 Nikolaus Harnoncourt was its conductor. In 1988 the ensemble was reformed with younger players, under the artistic direction of the oboist Bart Schneemann.

Today the ensemble plays in the Concertgebouw, Paradiso and the Muziekgebouw aan 't IJ and tours abroad. It makes its own programmes around a single composer or soloist, with, for example, Kevin Volans, Theo Loevendie, Guus Janssen, Ayub Ogada, the Hilliard Ensemble and Jordi Savall. Its records include Rossini for Wind, Arrangements for Wind and an arrangement of West Side Story. The ensemble shows how much colour and space a group of wind players can have.
artiest/nederlands-blazers-ensemble.listen: Listen to Rossini for Wind and notice how an operatic melody, which you normally know from singers, is taken over by oboe, clarinet, bassoon and horn.

artiest/nederlands-kamerkoor.text:
The Nederlands Kamerkoor (Netherlands Chamber Choir) is a Dutch choir with Utrecht as its administrative base, which gives concerts in various Dutch cities. Felix de Nobel founded it in 1937 as Chorus Pro Musica, to sing Bach cantatas for the broadcasting association VARA. In 1939 it performed in public for the first time in Haarlem, under the name Nederlandsch Kamerkoor. After the Second World War it toured England in 1948, Perugia in 1949 and in 1951 the Edinburgh Festival. That same year it received its first government subsidy, which became a permanent subsidy in 1953.

De Nobel stopped in 1972. His successor Hans van den Hombergh brought more historical performance practice to the choir, and Kerry Woodward led it from 1977 to 1980. After that it had no permanent conductor until 1988 and worked with guest conductors from the early music movement, such as Gustav Leonhardt, Nikolaus Harnoncourt, Ton Koopman, Christopher Hogwood and William Christie. In 1988 Uwe Gronostay came as chief conductor, until 1997. Since 2015 Peter Dijkstra has been chief conductor.

Composers such as Francis Poulenc, Frank Martin, Rudolf Escher, Hendrik Andriessen, Mauricio Kagel, John Tavener and Henk Badings wrote for the choir. Its records include the Requiem in D minor by Mozart, the Mass in B minor by Bach and Via Crucis. The choir shows how the Netherlands, from Bach to new work, built a choral culture of its own.
artiest/nederlands-kamerkoor.listen: Listen to the Requiem in D minor, KV. 626 and notice how the voices come together softly and broadly at the beginning, and how clearly you can follow each voice separately.

artiest/neil-sedaka.text:
Neil Sedaka (1939 to 2026) was an American singer, songwriter and pianist. He was born in Brooklyn and grew up in Brighton Beach, across from Neil Diamond, and he had a relationship with Carole King. His mother took a part-time job to buy him a second-hand piano, after his teacher had suggested giving him piano lessons. In 1947 he passed an audition for a piano scholarship.

Sedaka began his music career in 1957. He was briefly a co-founder of the doo-wop group The Tokens and then had a series of hits, above all with the lyricist Howard Greenfield: Oh! Carol in 1959, Calendar Girl in 1960, Happy Birthday Sweet Sixteen in 1961 and Breaking Up Is Hard to Do in 1962. In the mid-1960s his popularity declined, but in 1975 he made a comeback with two number 1s on the American Billboard Hot 100, Laughter in the Rain and Bad Blood. For these he worked mainly with the lyricist Phil Cody. Records such as Solitaire and The Hungry Years also appeared at that time.

Sedaka wrote or co-wrote more than five hundred songs, also for others, such as Stupid Cupid for Connie Francis, (Is This the Way to) Amarillo for Tony Christie and Love Will Keep Us Together for Captain & Tennille. In 1983 he was inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame. He kept performing, even during the Covid years with short concerts on social media. His melodic pop songs link the rock 'n' roll of the 1950s with the singer-songwriter era of the 1970s.
artiest/neil-sedaka.listen: Listen to Breaking Up Is Hard to Do and notice how cheerful and singable the melody is, while the lyrics are about a break-up.

artiest/neil-tennant.text:
Neil Tennant is the singer and lyricist of the Pet Shop Boys. He was born in 1954 in North Shields and grew up in Newcastle, where as a teenager he acted in a youth theatre, taught himself guitar and started a small folk group. From 1972 he studied history in London. He then worked at publishers, including Marvel UK, and from 1982 at the pop magazine Smash Hits, where he was news editor and interviewed, among others, Madonna.

In August 1981 Tennant met Chris Lowe, and the two began writing songs together as Pet Shop Boys. In New York Tennant met the producer Bobby Orlando, who made a first version of West End Girls in 1984. In 1985 the duo signed with Parlophone and Tennant left Smash Hits. Up to 1988 four number 1 hits followed in England. Tennant himself coined the term imperial phase for such a period in which an artist seems able to do no wrong.

Tennant writes most of the duo's lyrics. They are full of literary and political references and are set to dance music. He sings in a dry, detached manner, and sometimes speaks his lyrics more than he sings them. In It's a Sin he worked in memories of his schooldays. In 1994 he told the magazine Attitude that he is gay. He also sang with Electronic, including on Getting Away with It, and in 2018 his book One Hundred Lyrics and a Poem was published.
artiest/neil-tennant.listen: In West End Girls, listen to the verses, in which Tennant speaks his lyrics more than he sings them, almost like a rapper. Notice the cool, calm tone of his voice above the deep bass line and the synthesizers.

artiest/neil-young.text:
Neil Young is a Canadian-American singer-songwriter and guitarist, born in 1945 in Toronto. He grew up partly in Winnipeg and played in bands there as a teenager. In 1966 he moved to Los Angeles, where he co-founded Buffalo Springfield, a group that stood at the origin of folk rock and country rock.

In 1969 his solo album Everybody Knows This Is Nowhere was released, recorded with the band Crazy Horse. That same year he joined Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young. As a solo artist he made After the Gold Rush (1970) and Harvest (1972), with Heart of Gold, his only number 1 hit. Young sings with a high tenor and alternates between two sides: restrained folk and country songs and loud rock with Crazy Horse, full of distorted electric guitar. That second side earned him the nickname Godfather of Grunge. Rust Never Sleeps (1979) and Ragged Glory (1990) inspired later alternative bands, and in 1995 he made Mirror Ball with Pearl Jam.

Young also wrote songs about social issues. In Southern Man and Alabama he criticised racism in the southern United States. Lynyrd Skynyrd answered in 1974 with Sweet Home Alabama, in which Young is mentioned by name; he himself said he was a fan of the band. Young was inducted twice into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, in 1995 as a solo artist and in 1997 with Buffalo Springfield. He is a co-founder of Farm Aid, which supports American farming families.
artiest/neil-young.listen: In Southern Man (1970), listen to Young's electric guitar playing: sharp, raw solos between the verses. Notice the piano driving the rhythm and how the tension in the song keeps rising.

artiest/nelson-riddle.text:
Nelson Riddle (1921 to 1985) was an American arranger, composer, bandleader and orchestrator, active from the late 1940s to the mid-1980s. He was born in Oradell, New Jersey, and had piano lessons at the age of eight and trombone lessons at fourteen. An important experience was hearing Ravel's Boléro played by the Boston Symphony Orchestra under Serge Koussevitzky, of which he later said it was as if the orchestra leapt off the stage and hit you in the face. He wanted to become a jazz trombonist, but lacked the coordination for it, and so he turned to arranging. In Rumson he learned from Bill Finegan, who strongly influenced his arranging style.

At Capitol Records Riddle worked with many singers, including Frank Sinatra, Ella Fitzgerald, Nat King Cole, Judy Garland, Dean Martin, Peggy Lee, Johnny Mathis, Rosemary Clooney and Keely Smith. On records such as Frank Sinatra Sings for Only the Lonely from 1958, his orchestration gave the singing an atmosphere of its own. He also wrote and arranged music for many films and television series, and won an Oscar and three Grammys.

In the 1980s he found a new audience with three platinum albums with Linda Ronstadt. Riddle shows how much of the sound of 1950s popular singing lay with the arranger: strings and winds that made a world of their own around the voice, from swinging to deeply melancholy.
artiest/nelson-riddle.listen: Listen to Frank Sinatra Sings for Only the Lonely and notice how the strings and winds create a sombre atmosphere beneath the voice, without drowning out the singer.

artiest/nena.text:
Nena was a West German pop group from West Berlin, founded in 1982 and named after the singer Gabriele Kerner, who called herself Nena. She came from Hagen and had previously sung English-language new wave in the band The Stripes. At the suggestion of the record company CBS she moved to Berlin and began singing in German. There, with the drummer Rolf Brendel, the keyboardist Uwe Fahrenkrog-Petersen, the guitarist Carlo Karges and the bassist Jürgen Dehmel, she formed the group Nena, a band of the Neue Deutsche Welle.

The first single, Nur geträumt (1982), became a number 2 hit in West Germany after a performance on the TV programme Musikladen. In March 1983 came 99 Luftballons, with music by Fahrenkrog-Petersen and lyrics by Karges. Karges got the idea in June 1982, when he saw balloons rising into the sky at a Rolling Stones concert in West Berlin. The song begins quietly and then speeds up into a cheerful pop song with synthesizers and guitar, while the lyrics are about a nuclear war. It reached number 1 in West Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium and Austria and, in German, reached number 2 in the United States. The English version, 99 Red Balloons, reached number 1 in England.

The band itself was never happy with that English version, which made it too explicitly a protest song. After the albums Feuer und Flamme (1985) and Eisbrecher (1986) the group broke up in 1987. Nena's duet Anyplace, Anywhere, Anytime with Kim Wilde (2003) reached number 1 in the Netherlands. 99 Luftballons belongs, along with Two Tribes and De bom, to the pop songs that cheerfully packaged the fear of the bomb in the 1980s.
artiest/nena.listen: In 99 Luftballons, notice the build-up: the song begins slowly, with only voice and soft keyboards, and then shifts into a fast beat with a pumping bass. The cheerful, danceable music is at odds with the lyrics, which end with the singer alone in the ruins.

artiest/nerija.text:
Nérija is a British jazz collective from London, best known for its album Blume from 2019. There is little to be found about the group itself in our source material. That source file is about one of its members, the saxophonist Nubya Garcia, and it says a lot about the world from which the collective emerges.

Garcia was born in 1991 in Camden Town in London and learned violin and viola as a child. At the age of ten she began on saxophone. She played in the Camden Jazz Band, followed the youth programme of the Royal Academy of Music and attended workshops at the Roundhouse and at Tomorrow's Warriors. In 2016 she graduated from Trinity Laban, in the same class as Joe Armon-Jones and Moses Boyd. In 2017 her debut EP Nubya's 5ive was released. In 2018 followed When We Are, with which she explored how electronics can be used in a live jazz setting. She is also a member of the Afro-jazz ensemble Maisha.

Nérija belongs to the new wave of London jazz, in which young musicians got to know one another through youth programmes and conservatoires and formed groups together. The jazz of this generation is open to African and Caribbean influences and to electronics.
artiest/nerija.listen: Listen to a track from Blume and notice how the horns and the rhythm section give each other space, so that the solos sound like conversations.

artiest/neu.text:
Neu! was a West German band from Düsseldorf that began in 1971 with two musicians who had just left Kraftwerk: the drummer Klaus Dinger and the guitarist Michael Rother. Together with the producer Conny Plank, who in the krautrock world was called the hidden third member, they recorded three albums: Neu! in 1972, Neu! 2 in 1973 and Neu! '75 in 1975. After that the band broke up. In the mid-1980s they briefly returned, and later two more records appeared with material from that time.

The name came from the advertising world of Düsseldorf. Dinger considered new the strongest word in advertising. The cover of the first album was inspired by the pop art of Andy Warhol. The record sold little at first. The band's trademark is the motorik, a minimalist rhythm in 4/4 time that Dinger developed together with Jaki Liebezeit. The rhythm runs tight and unceasing, like a car driving along an empty motorway. On Neu! 2 the money for the recordings ran out, and the band filled the second side with processed versions of the single Neuschnee and Super, played back at different speeds. That is regarded as one of the earliest examples of a remix.

Commercially Neu! amounted to little, but in retrospect the group is regarded as one of the core bands of 1970s German krautrock. Their influence extends to electronic music and to punk. Drummers such as Stephen Morris of Joy Division also name Dinger as an example.
artiest/neu.listen: Listen to Hallogallo from 1972. Tap along with the rhythm and notice how the track above all keeps rolling forward, without major turns.

artiest/neville-marriner.text:
Sir Neville Marriner (1924 to 2016) was an English conductor and violinist. He was born in Lincoln, the son of a carpenter, and played in a jazz band at school with the composer Steve Race. He learned violin and piano from his father. In 1939 he went to the Royal College of Music in London. He served in the army in 1941, but was discharged in 1943 because of kidney problems, and then also studied at the Conservatoire de Paris.

Marriner taught briefly at Eton College and in 1948 became a professor at the Royal College of Music. He played second violin for thirteen years in the Martin String Quartet, and in the Jacobean Ensemble of the harpsichordist Thurston Dart. He then played violin with the Philharmonia Orchestra and the London Symphony Orchestra, where he was principal second violin from 1954 to 1969.

He founded the Academy of St Martin in the Fields. His collaboration with that orchestra is the most recorded of any orchestra with a conductor. Records such as The Four Seasons from 1970, Serenade for Strings and Concertos For Oboe And Strings stand for the clear, supple sound of the chamber orchestra. Gramophone counts him among the fifty best conductors. In this way he became one of the best-known conductors in the world, because his recordings made Baroque and Classical music accessible to a large audience.
artiest/neville-marriner.listen: Listen to The Four Seasons in Marriner's recording and notice how clearly the solo violin rises above the strings.

artiest/new-cool-collective.text:
New Cool Collective is a Dutch group founded in 1993. The core consists of the saxophonist Benjamin Herman, the drummer Joost Kroon, the percussionists Frank van Dok and Jos de Haas, the keyboardist and arranger Willem Friede, the bassist Leslie Lopez and the trumpeter David Rockefeller. In addition there is a big band of nineteen musicians, with an extensive horn section of saxophones, trumpets and trombones, plus guitar, Fender Rhodes, percussion and vocals. The group has performed in many countries, from Hungary and Russia to Uganda and Japan, and was often seen on Dutch television.

The first records, More! and Soul Jazz Latin, appeared in 1997. In 2000 the band won the Edison Jazz Award, and in 2018 it received another for New Cool Collective Big Band, on which the Senegalese saxophonist Thierno Koité can also be heard. For the music for the film Toegetakeld door de liefde the group won a Golden Calf in 2013. That music is on the album Chin Chin. They also made Hollandse Meesters (2014), with arrangements of Dutch evergreens, together with Guus Meeuwis.

The name indicates what the band plays: jazz that draws directly on soul, Latin and Afrobeat. In 2006 it travelled the club circuit with the drummer Tony Allen and the kora player Ali Boulo Santo for an Afrobeat tour. For Dutch pop history the group is important because it shows that jazz in the Netherlands can also have a danceable, broad side. In the course it appears with Scuzzy Skank from 2008.
artiest/new-cool-collective.listen: Listen to Scuzzy Skank. Try to follow the horns, the percussion and the bass separately and notice how together they form a danceable whole.

artiest/new-order.text:
New Order is an English band from Manchester, founded in 1980. The singer and guitarist Bernard Sumner, the bassist Peter Hook and the drummer Stephen Morris had previously played in Joy Division. They had agreed not to use that name any more if one of them dropped out. After the suicide of the singer Ian Curtis they therefore continued under a new name. Shortly afterwards the keyboardist Gillian Gilbert joined. Sumner became the new singer, although he found singing and playing guitar at the same time difficult. The band became the figurehead of the label Factory Records and its associated club The Haçienda, and Peter Saville designed their sleeves.

The debut album Movement (1981) still sounded dark, like Joy Division. During visits to New York the band discovered the club music of the time: electro, freestyle and Italian disco. Morris taught himself to program drum machines. In 1983 came Blue Monday, a fully electronically programmed track with a four-on-the-floor beat, inspired by disco. It became the best-selling independent twelve-inch single in Britain. That same year Power, Corruption & Lies was released, on which guitars, bass and synthesizers came together. Low-Life (1985), Brotherhood (1986) and Technique (1989) followed.

New Order brought post-punk and electronic dance music together and so became a forerunner of alternative dance music. Hook's melodic bass guitar, the sequencers and Sumner's cool vocals were imitated by other bands well into the 1990s. After a break in the 1990s the group carried on, in 2007 without Hook. In 2026 Joy Division and New Order were inducted together into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
artiest/new-order.listen: Listen to Blue Monday. Notice the drum machine at the beginning with its stuttering bass drum, and how after that synthesizers and a melodic bass guitar come in layer by layer.

artiest/new-orleans-rhythm-kings.text:
The New Orleans Rhythm Kings were a jazz band of the early 1920s, formed by musicians from New Orleans and Chicago. It began with a telegram from the drummer Mike Stevens to Albert Brunies, about better gigs in Chicago. The trumpeter Paul Mares seized the chance, the trombonist George Brunies followed, and in Chicago they were joined by, among others, the pianist Elmer Schoebel, the saxophonist Jack Pettis and the clarinettist Leon Roppolo. In 1921 the group got a regular place at Friar's Inn, where it kept playing for seventeen months. The name New Orleans Rhythm Kings had first belonged to a group of the vaudeville performer Bee Palmer.

In 1922 and 1923 they made records for Gennett Records in Richmond, Indiana, at first still under the name Friar's Society Orchestra. In July 1923 Jelly Roll Morton played on one of their sessions. From their repertoire came jazz standards such as Bugle Call Rag, Milenburg Joys, Farewell Blues and Tin Roof Blues. The pop song Make Love to Me from 1954 is based on the last-named piece.

The band wanted to present jazz more seriously and carefully than the popular Original Dixieland Jazz Band, which presented itself mainly as an entertaining novelty. Young musicians, among them the cornettist Bix Beiderbecke, came to Friar's Inn to listen and sometimes to play along. After Friar's Inn the group broke up and came together only to record, with Mares and Roppolo as the permanent core. Its influence on Chicago jazz and on a younger generation of musicians makes it an important link between New Orleans and the jazz of the 1920s.
artiest/new-orleans-rhythm-kings.listen: Listen to Tin Roof Blues and notice how clarinet, cornet and trombone play in and out of one another, without any one of them pulling the piece entirely towards itself. Then look up Make Love to Me and hear how the melody returns in that pop song.

artiest/new-york-philharmonic.text:
The New York Philharmonic is a symphony orchestra from New York and one of the oldest musical institutions in the United States. The conductor Ureli Corelli Hill founded the orchestra in 1842, with the help of the Irish composer William Vincent Wallace, as the Philharmonic Society of New York. The first concert took place on 7 December 1842 in the Apollo Rooms on Broadway, for some six hundred listeners, and opened with Beethoven's Fifth Symphony. In 1846 the orchestra gave the American premiere of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony. It is one of the so-called Big Five of the American orchestras and today plays in David Geffen Hall at Lincoln Center.

In the nineteenth century the conductors often changed. Afterwards conductors such as Theodore Thomas set the level of the orchestra. In 1878 a rival emerged with Leopold Damrosch's Symphony Society of New York, and Walter Damrosch persuaded Andrew Carnegie to build a new concert hall, which opened in 1891.

For anyone studying pop and jazz, this orchestra is interesting above all as a link with the classical world. The orchestra's records, including from the 1950s and 1960s, feature works such as Le Sacre du printemps, Scheherazade and Rhapsody in Blue. There is also Bernstein Plays Brubeck Plays Bernstein from 1960, an album on which the world of the symphony orchestra and that of jazz meet. The New York Rock & Roll Ensemble also played with the orchestra at Leonard Bernstein's invitation.
artiest/new-york-philharmonic.listen: Listen to Le Sacre du printemps in one of the orchestra's recordings and notice the rhythmic force of the winds and the percussion. Ask yourself how a symphony orchestra can produce such pulsating, almost rock-like energy.

artiest/new-york-rock-en-roll-ensemble.text:
The New York Rock & Roll Ensemble was a rock band of the late 1960s and early 1970s, whose music was described as classical baroque rock. The group came together around the Juilliard students Michael Kamen, Marty Fulterman (later known as Mark Snow) and Dorian Rudnytsky, joined by the rock musicians Brian Corrigan and Clif Nivison. After a first performance at a Juilliard Halloween ball in 1967 they signed with Atlantic Records. They performed in white tie and tails.

Their debut album The New York Rock & Roll Ensemble was released in 1968 and used classical instruments in rock songs and rock instruments in classical pieces. Leonard Bernstein invited them to one of his Young People's Concerts with the New York Philharmonic. There they played their best-known piece, Brandenburg, based on the first movement of Bach's Brandenburg Concerto No. 5. The piece begins as an ordinary performance with two oboes, guitar and cello and then turns into a rock song. Faithful Friends and Reflections followed, both in 1969, and on Columbia Roll Over in 1971, their most rock-oriented album. It includes Fields of Joy, which Lenny Kravitz covered in 1991. Freedomburger from 1972 was their last record.

The band remained small, but its members made careers. Kamen became known for film music and for projects in which classical music and rock came together, Snow for music for television series, above all The X Files. The group shows how early attempts were already made to link classical and popular music.
artiest/new-york-rock-en-roll-ensemble.listen: Listen to Brandenburg and notice the moment at which the strict Baroque performance turns into a rock song. Hear how Bach's melody keeps sounding.

artiest/new-zealand-symphony-orchestra.text:
The New Zealand Symphony Orchestra, in Maori Te Tira Pūoro o Aotearoa, is the national orchestra of New Zealand and is based in Wellington. The idea of a national orchestra had existed since 1925, when the Radio Broadcasting Company was founded. In 1939 an orchestra came together for the Centennial Exhibition of 1940. After the Second World War it became a permanent ensemble in 1946, as the National Orchestra of the New Zealand Broadcasting Service. The first concert took place on 6 March 1947. In 1961 Igor Stravinsky and his assistant Robert Craft conducted the orchestra in a programme of Stravinsky's work.

The name changed in 1963 to NZBC Symphony Orchestra and in 1975 to New Zealand Symphony Orchestra. Since 1988 the orchestra has been independent of Radio New Zealand and operates as a state-owned enterprise. The concerts are still recorded and broadcast by Radio New Zealand Concert. The orchestra plays in Wellington, Auckland, Christchurch and Dunedin.

On record the orchestra has played a wide repertoire, from Liszt and Stravinsky to Britten and Hindemith, and also work by New Zealand composers, as on the albums New Zealand Composers from 1995 and Aotearoa from 1997. For pop and jazz the orchestra is above all an example of how a national orchestra also serves lighter music: Beauty Spot and Beauty Spot II from 2000 and 2001, Espresso Guitar Two and Warriors From Pluto from 2001 belong to its discography.
artiest/new-zealand-symphony-orchestra.listen: Listen to a piece by the orchestra from the album Aotearoa or New Zealand Composers and notice how the orchestral sound comes across in New Zealand music. Ask yourself which colours strike you first.

artiest/ngoni-ba.text:
Ngoni Ba is a group from Mali, led by the ngoni player Bassekou Kouyaté. The name refers to the instrument at its centre: the ngoni, a traditional West African stringed instrument with a wooden or calabash body over which a dried animal skin is stretched. The instrument has been known since at least 1352, when the Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta saw one at the court of Mansa Musa. It is regarded as related to the akonting and the xalam and as a forerunner of the banjo in North America.

The group released five albums: Segu Blue in 2006, I Speak Fula in 2009, Jama Ko in 2013, Ba Power in 2015 and Miri in 2019. On those records the ngoni is not accompaniment but the lead instrument. Griots traditionally played the ngoni at celebrations and special occasions, and the fast melodic lines that the instrument can produce are given room in Ngoni Ba, with the rhythmic power of a band behind them.

The group shows how an old Malian tradition can live in a contemporary band format. In this way it fits in the line of West African music that connects blues lovers and world music fans, and that shows how closely related the stringed instruments of Mali and the banjo are.
artiest/ngoni-ba.listen: Listen to a track from Segu Blue and notice the ngoni: how fast and melodic can this instrument play, and what do the other instruments around it do? See whether you can hear the old griot tradition in the playing style.

artiest/nicholas-britell.text: Nicholas Britell was born in New York in 1980. He received classical piano training at the Juilliard pre-college programme, studied at Harvard and played there in an instrumental hip hop group. Those two worlds come together in his music. For Barry Jenkins's Moonlight (2016) he applied a hip hop technique, slowing down and lowering the pitch of a recording, to classical string music. In If Beale Street Could Talk (2018) he wrote lush strings and horns for a love story in Harlem. The title music of Succession (2018) sets classical piano and strings on a heavy hip hop beat and won an Emmy. For the Star Wars series Andor (2022) he designed a new sound world of his own.
artiest/nicholas-britell.listen: Notice the slowed, lowered string sound in Moonlight: a hip hop technique that makes classical music dreamy and heavy.

artiest/nick-cave.text:
Nick Cave was born in 1957 in the small Australian town of Warracknabeal, in the state of Victoria. He studied art in Melbourne and sang there in The Birthday Party, one of the best post-punk bands in the city. In 1980 the group moved to London, and after a stay in West Berlin it broke up in 1982. The following year Cave founded Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds, a band that would last for decades. He is also a writer: his first novel, And the Ass Saw the Angel, appeared in 1989.

His music revolves around a deep baritone voice and themes such as death, religion, love and violence. The first Bad Seeds records are set in a mythical American South, with influences from spirituals and Delta blues. The Mercy Seat from 1988 is regarded as his most important song. In the 1990s he broke through with quieter, piano-led ballads, such as the duet with Kylie Minogue, Where the Wild Roses Grow, in 1996 and Into My Arms in 1997.

From the 2000s he increasingly wrote film music, often with Warren Ellis, including for The Proposition, The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford and Hell or High Water. In 2019 Ghosteen was released, after the death of his son Arthur. The course shows him from the angle of the music video: in 1992 an artist directed the video of Straight to You for him, an example of how image and music reinforced each other in the 1990s. Cave was appointed Officer of the Order of Australia in 2017.
artiest/nick-cave.listen: Listen to Where the Wild Roses Grow, his duet with Kylie Minogue. Notice how his low voice and her light voice stand in contrast.

artiest/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds.text:
Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds is an Australian rock band, formed in 1983 by the singer Nick Cave, the multi-instrumentalist Mick Harvey and the German guitarist and singer Blixa Bargeld. It arose after the break-up of The Birthday Party, the group of Cave and Harvey, who knew each other from a boarding school in Melbourne. A first version came together in London in September 1983 as a backing band for Cave's planned solo project Man or Myth?. At first the group was called Nick Cave and the Cavemen. In May 1984 that became Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds, after The Birthday Party's last EP, The Bad Seed. The bassist Barry Adamson of Magazine was part of the first regular line-up, and later, among others, Kid Congo Powers and Warren Ellis joined.

The debut album From Her to Eternity was released in 1984. In the 1980s the band leaned on post-punk, blues and gothic rock. Later the sound became softer and other influences came in, as on The Good Son from 1990 and The Boatman's Call from 1997. Other albums are Let Love In (1994), Murder Ballads (1996), Push the Sky Away (2013), Skeleton Tree (2016), Ghosteen (2019) and Wild God (2024). After Harvey left in 2009 the sound became more spacious, with electronic and ambient colours.

The band is regarded as one of the most idiosyncratic groups of the post-punk and alternative rock era. It constantly changed its line-up and showed that an established rock band can reinvent itself time and again, with lyrics that are often about death, faith and love.
artiest/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds.listen: Listen to a track from The Boatman's Call and notice how soft and restrained it sounds, with Nick Cave's voice close to the piano. Compare that with a track from From Her to Eternity and hear how much rawer the band began.

artiest/nick-cave-en-warren-ellis.text: Nick Cave (1957, Warracknabeal) and Warren Ellis (1965, Ballarat) both come from Australia. Cave became known with the post-punk band The Birthday Party and in 1983 founded Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds. Ellis started the group Dirty Three in 1992 and shortly afterwards became a member of the Bad Seeds. He plays, among other instruments, violin, viola, piano and accordion. For The Proposition (2005), a Western in the Australian outback, Cave wrote the screenplay and together they made the music. Among others, The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford (2007), The Road (2009), Hell or High Water (2016) and Wind River (2017) followed. Ellis received a César in 2016 for his music for Mustang.
artiest/nick-cave-en-warren-ellis.listen: Notice the bare line-up of piano, violin and celesta, with short motifs that are often repeated and little harmonic movement, like a landscape that stays still.

artiest/nick-drake.text:
Nick Drake was born on 19 June 1948 in Rangoon in Burma, the son of an English engineer. In 1951 the family returned to England, to Tanworth-in-Arden in Warwickshire. His mother wrote songs herself and encouraged him; he learned piano, clarinet and saxophone and played at school in a band with R&B and jazz standards. In 1967 he began a degree in English literature at Cambridge. There, before he had finished, he signed with Island Records at the age of twenty. He made the recordings for his debut alongside his studies.

His first album Five Leaves Left was released in 1969, followed by Bryter Layter in 1971 and Pink Moon in 1972. Drake was an excellent acoustic guitarist and his songs have a vulnerable, restrained tone. He suffered from depression and was reluctant to perform. After Pink Moon he withdrew from recording and performing and went to live with his parents again. On 25 November 1974 he died at the age of twenty-six from an overdose of antidepressants.

During his lifetime he reached very few listeners. Recognition came only after his death. The compilation Fruit Tree from 1979 ensured that his work was listened to again, and many later artists cite him as an influence. His name today stands for the quiet, personal side of the folk of the 1960s and 1970s, the opposite of the big stages of rock.
artiest/nick-drake.listen: Listen to a track from Pink Moon and notice the combination of acoustic guitar and soft voice. Hear how little is needed to create so much atmosphere.
